title: Trading Desks to Clinical Trials: Parallels in Applied Vertical AI — Ayush Bhardwaj, Allos AI
talk_summary: A practitioner compares applied AI at a hedge fund and a pharma startup and argues the build recipe is identical: narrow problem framing, proprietary data curation, prompt modeling, observability, then a human-expert-driven learning loop. The core claim is that model/infra is commodity and domain-expert judgment encoded into prompts, data, and rubrics is the only durable edge.

takeaways.technique: Domain-expert-in-the-loop error analysis before any fine-tuning
takeaways.what_they_do: Hire the actual user (trader/scientist) to read traces, judge outputs, refine prompts, and curate data; treat plain log error analysis as the highest-ROI improvement step before SFT/RLHF.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the cheapest of all and I think the highest ROI is the error analysis ... you just analyze the logs plain and simple

takeaways.what_they_do: Humans author explicit rubrics; an AI grader scores outputs against the rubric to drive iteration, but they warn this can become an echo chamber if the grader shares the generator's blind spots.
takeaways.evidence_quote: human can just create a rubric and then AI will just like grade itself based on that rubric ... you might run into an echo chamber

takeaways.technique: Narrow single-purpose agents over one generalist
takeaways.what_they_do: Decompose the job into narrow, pointed tasks and build many small agents rather than one agent doing everything.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you need to pick a very narrow task ... Last I checked there was no tax on building more AI agents

takeaways.technique: Encode expert mental model as ordered steps
takeaways.what_they_do: Write prompts that mirror how a domain expert actually solves the task, as an explicit ordered procedure rather than a vague goal.

takeaways.technique: Curate proprietary failure data as the moat
takeaways.what_they_do: Deliberately capture the data competitors/LLMs lack — failed experiments, trade theses — and structure it with LLM workflows so it feeds future reasoning.
takeaways.evidence_quote: in pharma it is the data for failed experiments because successful experiments data yes you can get it but failed experiments that's relatively hard

takeaways.technique: Human-in-the-loop over full autonomy for judgment tasks
takeaways.what_they_do: Keep experts deciding among AI-generated candidates (AI-in-the-loop) rather than removing humans, because models do text statistics not causal world models.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's AITL AI in the loop cuz everything is like done by the expert but the AI assistant really helps save time
